arxiv-1808-10105.title: OWLAx: A Protégé Plugin to Support Ontology Axiomatization through Diagramming
arxiv-1808-10105.creator: Md. Kamruzzaman Sarker, Adila A. Krisnadhi, Pascal Hitzler
arxiv-1808-10105.description: Abstract Once the conceptual overview, in terms of a somewhat informal class diagram, has been designed in the course of engineering an ontology, the process of adding many of the appropriate logical axioms is mostly a routine task. We provide a Protégé 1 1 1 http://protege.stanford.

arxiv-2102-00722.title: Elastic electron-proton scattering in the presence of a circularly polarized laser field
arxiv-2102-00722.creator: I Dahiri, M Jakha, S Mouslih, B Manaut, S Taj
arxiv-2102-00722.description: Abstract Owing to recent advances in laser technology, it has become important to investigate fundamental laser-assisted processes in very powerful laser fields. In the present work and within the framework of laser-assisted quantum electrodynamics (QED), electron-proton scattering was considered in the presence of a strong electromagnetic field of circular polarization.

arxiv-2102-01350.title: Graph Coarsening with Neural Networks
arxiv-2102-01350.creator: Chen Cai, Dingkang Wang, Yusu Wang
arxiv-2102-01350.description: Abstract As large-scale graphs become increasingly more prevalent, it poses significant computational challenges to process, extract and analyze large graph data. Graph coarsening is one popular technique to reduce the size of a graph while maintaining essential properties. Despite rich graph coarsening literature, there is only limited exploration of data-driven methods in the field.

arxiv-2103-01250.title: Mobility driven coexistence of living organisms Journal: Physica A
arxiv-2103-01250.creator: B.F. de Oliveira, M.V. de Moraes, D. Bazeia, and A. Szolnoki
arxiv-2103-01250.description: Abstract We propose a minimal off-lattice model of living organisms where just a very few dynamical rules of growth are assumed. The stable coexistence of many clusters is detected when we replace the global restriction rule by a locally applied one. A rich variety of evolving patterns is revealed where players movement has a decisive role on the evolutionary outcome.

arxiv-2103-06422.title: Holistic 3D Scene Understanding from a Single Image with Implicit Representation
arxiv-2103-06422.creator: Cheng Zhang 2∗ Zhaopeng Cui 1∗ Yinda Zhang 3 Bing Zeng 2 Marc Pollefeys 4 Shuaicheng Liu 2 1 State Key Lab of CAD & CG, Zhejiang University 2 University of Electronic Science and Technology of China 3 Google 4 ETH Zürich
arxiv-2103-06422.description: Abstract We present a new pipeline for holistic 3D scene understanding from a single image, which could predict object shapes, object poses, and scene layout. As it is a highly ill-posed problem, existing methods usually suffer from inaccurate estimation of both shapes and layout especially for the cluttered scene due to the heavy occlusion between objects.

arxiv-2201-10419.title: Ensemble Learning Priors Driven Deep Unfolding for Scalable Video Snapshot Compressive Imaging
arxiv-2201-10419.creator: Chengshuai Yang, Shiyu Zhang, Xin Yuan✉
arxiv-2201-10419.description: Abstract Snapshot compressive imaging (SCI) can record a 3D datacube by a 2D measurement and algorithmically reconstruct the desired 3D information from that 2D measurement. The reconstruction algorithm thus plays a vital role in SCI. Recently, deep learning (DL) has demonstrated outstanding performance in reconstruction, leading to better results than conventional optimization-based methods.

arxiv-2209-14301.title: Beating stellar systematic error floors using transit-based densities Facilities: Exoplanet Archive, Gaia, FLWO:2MASS, CTIO:2MASS, WISE
arxiv-2209-14301.creator: Jason D. Eastman, Hannah Diamond-Lowe, Jamie Tayar
arxiv-2209-14301.description: Abstract It has long been understood that the light curve of a transiting planet constrains the density of its host star. That fact is routinely used to improve measurements of the stellar surface gravity and has been argued to be an independent check on the stellar mass.

arxiv-2305-19909.title: The effect of spatial sampling on the resolution of the magnetostatic inverse problem
arxiv-2305-19909.creator: Jussi Nurminen, Andrey Zhdanov, Wan Jin Yeo, Joonas Iivanainen, Julia Stephen
arxiv-2305-19909.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jussi Nurminen, Andrey Zhdanov, Wan Jin Yeo, Joonas Iivanainen, Julia Stephen. In magnetoencephalography, linear minimum norm inverse methods are commonly employed when a solution with minimal a priori assumptions is desirable. These methods typically produce spatially extended inverse solutions, even when the generating source is focal. Various reasons have been proposed for this effect, including intrisic properties of the minimum norm solution, effects of regularization, noise, and limitations of the sensor array.

arxiv-2402-11350.title: Non-Heisenbergian Quantum Mechanics
arxiv-2402-11350.creator: MohammadJavad Kazemi, Ghadir Jafari
arxiv-2402-11350.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by MohammadJavad Kazemi, Ghadir Jafari. Relaxing the postulates of an axiomatic theory is a natural way to find more general theories, and historically, the discovery of non-Euclidean geometry is a famous example of this procedure. Here, we use this way to extend quantum mechanics by ignoring the heart of Heisenberg’s quantum mechanics—We do not assume the existence of a position operator that satisfies the Heisenberg commutation relation, [ x ^ , p ^ ] = i ​ ℏ [\hat{x},\hat{p}]=i\hbar .

arxiv-2406-07146.title: Argus: Benchmarking and Enhancing Vision-Language Models for 3D Radiology Report Generation
arxiv-2406-07146.creator: Che Liu, Zhongwei Wan, Yuqi Wang, Hui Shen, Haozhe Wang, Kangyu Zheng, Mi Zhang, Rossella Arcucci
arxiv-2406-07146.description: Abstract Automatic radiology report generation holds significant potential to streamline the labor-intensive process of report writing by radiologists, particularly for 3D radiographs such as CT scans. While CT scans are critical for clinical diagnostics, they remain less explored compared to 2D radiographs.

arxiv-2406-18421.title: Neural Network Emulation of Flow in Heavy-Ion Collisions at Intermediate Energies
arxiv-2406-18421.creator: Nicholas Cox, Xavier Grundler, Bao-An Li
arxiv-2406-18421.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Nicholas Cox, Xavier Grundler, Bao-An Li. Applications of new techniques in machine learning are speeding up progress in research in various fields. In this work, we construct and evaluate a deep neural network (DNN) to be used within a Bayesian statistical framework as a faster and more reliable alternative to the Gaussian Process (GP) emulator of an isospin-dependent Boltzmann-Uehling-Uhlenbeck (IBUU) transport model simulator of heavy-ion reactions at intermediate beam energies.

The abstract framework and the main results of the paper were obtained by Poveda and Thei during a visit of the latter to Harvard University in the Sp

arxiv-2408-05973.description: Abstract . We construct a model of ZFC with a singular cardinal κ \kappa such that every subset of κ \kappa in L ⁡ ( V κ + 1 ) L(V_{\kappa+1}) has both the κ \kappa -Perfect Set Property and the 𝒰 → \mathcal{\vec{U}} -Baire Property.

arxiv-2511-18882.title: Facade Segmentation for Solar Photovoltaic Suitability
arxiv-2511-18882.creator: Ayca Duran, Christoph Waibel, Bernd Bickel, Iro Armeni, Arno Schlueter
arxiv-2511-18882.description: Abstract Building integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) facades represent a promising pathway towards urban decarbonization, especially where roof areas are insufficient and ground - mounted arrays are infeasible. Although machine learning-based approaches to support photovoltaic (PV) planning on rooftops are well researched, automated approaches for facades still remain scarce and oversimplified.

arxiv-2512-02280.title: Bridging the Gap: Toward Cognitive Autonomy in Artificial Intelligence
arxiv-2512-02280.creator: Noorbakhsh Amiri Golilarz, Sindhuja Penchala, Shahram Rahimi
arxiv-2512-02280.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Noorbakhsh Amiri Golilarz, Sindhuja Penchala, Shahram Rahimi. Artificial intelligence has advanced rapidly across perception, language, reasoning, and multimodal domains. Yet despite these achievements, modern AI systems remain fundamentally limited in their ability to self-monitor, self-correct, and regulate their behavior autonomously in dynamic contexts.

arxiv-2601-04722.title: Does Provenance Interact? [Vision Paper]
arxiv-2601-04722.creator: Chrysanthi Kosyfaki, Ruiyuan Zhang, Nikos Mamoulis, Xiaofang Zhou
arxiv-2601-04722.description: Abstract . Data provenance (the process of determining the origin and derivation of data outputs) has applications across multiple domains including explaining database query results and auditing scientific workflows. Despite decades of research, provenance tracing remains challenging due to computational costs and storage overhead.

arxiv-2601-05350.title: From compatibility of measurements to exploring Quantum Darwinism on NISQ
arxiv-2601-05350.creator: Emery Doucet, Sebastian Deffner
arxiv-2601-05350.description: Abstract Quantum Darwinism explains how tenets of classical reality, such as objectivity and repeatability, emerge within a quantum universe. As a mathematical framework, Quantum Darwinism also provides guiding principles that determine what physical models support emergent classical behavior, what specific observables obey classical laws, and much more.

arxiv-2602-14650.title: Data-Efficient Machine learning for Predicting Dopant Formation Energies in TiO 2 \text{TiO}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\smash[t]{\text{2}}} Monolayer
arxiv-2602-14650.creator: Kati Asikainen, Matti Alatalo, Marko Huttula, Assa Aravindh Sasikala Devi
arxiv-2602-14650.description: Abstract Machine learning models are increasingly applied in materials science, yet their predictive power is often constrained by data scarcity. Here, we show that accurate predictions can be achieved, even with a limited number of training examples, provided the dataset is compact and and grounded in physically relevant quantities.

plos-pone-0001292.creator: Claus Lamm, Howard C. Nusbaum, Andrew N. Meltzoff et al.
plos-pone-0001292.description: PLOS ONE research article. Recent neuroscientific evidence suggests that empathy for pain activates similar neural representations as the first-hand experience of pain. However, empathy is not an all-or-none phenomenon but it is strongly malleable by interpersonal, intrapersonal and situational factors. Th

pmc-11519888.title: Tumor-infiltrating immune cell profiles and changes associate with additional trastuzumab in preoperative chemotherapy for patients with HER2-positive gastric cancer
pmc-11519888.creator: Cong Chen, Jing Han, Qifei He, Qian Yao, Xueying Wang, Zuofu Peng, Yu Sun, Jiafu Ji, Xiaofang Xing
pmc-11519888.description: BackgroundHER2(+) gastric cancer (GC) can benefit from trastuzumab. However, the impact of additional trastuzumab in preoperative treatment on immune cells remains largely unknown.MethodsIn cohort I, immune cells were detected by immunohistochemistry in 1321 patients. Then 88 HER2(+) patients received preoperative therapy were collected as cohort II.

pmc-11568831.title: The Itappachi Universal Motion Platform for Accurate Dose Measurement in Thoracoabdominal Radiotherapy
pmc-11568831.creator: Naoki Tohyama, Eriko Saito, Kazuhide Uchida, Kiyoshi Yoda, Shinichiro Mori
pmc-11568831.description: We developed the “Itappachi” universal motion platform for measuring radiation doses under simulated respiratory motion in radiation therapy. The interplay effect, resulting from respiratory motion, degrades dose delivery precision in advanced treatments such as volumetric modulated arc therapy. The Itappachi platform is designed for precise dose measurement in dynamic scenarios through its ability to simulate respiratory motion.

pmc-11674372.title: Spinal Metastases in Non-Seminomatous Germ Cell Testicular Tumors: Prognosis and Integrated Therapeutic Approaches—A Systematic Review with an Institutional Case Illustration
pmc-11674372.creator: Gianluca Scalia, Gianluca Ferini, Zubayer Shams, Francesca Graziano, Giancarlo Ponzo, Eliana Giurato, Maria Grazia Galasso, Vitalinda Pumo, Martina Caruso, Gianluca Galvano, Salvatore Marrone, Jessica Naimo, Giovanni Federico Nicoletti, Giuseppe Emmanuele Umana
pmc-11674372.description: (1) Background: Testicular cancer, although accounting for only 0.5% to 1% of all solid male cancers, is the most common malignancy in males aged 15 to 35 years. Non-seminomatous germ cell tumors (NSGCT) represent nearly half of all testicular germ cell tumors and are associated with a more aggressive clinical course.

pmc-12619594.title: A Correlational Study on CALLY Index as a Potential Predictive Indicator for Postoperative in-Hospital Mortality in Acute Aortic Dissection Patients
pmc-12619594.creator: Hailun Zhang, Fei Jiang, Jingshan Lin, Xijing Yu, Yanchun Peng, Liangwan Chen, Yanjuan Lin
pmc-12619594.description: ObjectiveAcute Type A Aortic Dissection (ATAAD) is a highly lethal cardiovascular emergency characterized by persistently high postoperative in-hospital mortality (POIM), which necessitates effective preoperative risk assessment tools. This study aimed to investigate the predictive value of the preoperative CRP-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index for POIM in ATAAD patients and to construct a corresponding nomogram model.

pmc-13016714.title: Reproductive and Female Health in the Australian Defence Force 2002-2023: A Systematic Review and Synthesis
pmc-13016714.creator: Natasha Kinsman, Helen Kelsall, Dunya Tomic, Alex Collie, Zoe Jenkins, Jace Drain, Julian Saboisky, Karen Walker-Bone
pmc-13016714.description: IntroductionMilitary service involves potential exposure to a range of physical, chemical, and biological hazards that could impact reproductive health. Females represent 20% of Australian Defence Force (ADF) members and, like many military services, the ADF is prioritizing their recruitment and retention. However, given that females have different physiology and anthropometry, specific female occupational research is essential.

pmc-13062344.title: The mini chamber test: a novel bioassay for bioefficacy testing of chlorfenapyr treated nets used in malaria control
pmc-13062344.creator: Amy Lewis, Rowan Jones-Brown, Gemma Harvey, Giorgio Praulins, Emma Reid, Aidi Galus Lugenge, Frank Mechan, Katherine Gleave, Rosemary Susan Lees
pmc-13062344.description: Dual-active-ingredient insecticide-treated nets (Dual-AI ITNs) combining pyrethroids with chlorfenapyr are increasingly being deployed across malaria-endemic areas. Laboratory evaluation of chlorfenapyr ITNs is challenging due to chlorfenapyr’s requirement for metabolic activation.Inspired by the tunnel test, the mini chamber test is smaller, has higher throughput, and is animal-free.

pmc-13092578.title: Comparative performance of air sampling methods in a broiler house: implications for use and recovery of bacteria
pmc-13092578.creator: JT Porzeinski, LA Wythe, AP McElroy, MB Farnell
pmc-13092578.description: Accurate quantification of airborne bacteria in broiler houses is essential for assessing exposure risks to workers and animals, as well as for developing informed sanitation and surveillance strategies. Numerous sampling methods and equipment with differing collection physics, sampling parameters, processing, and handling have been developed in order to collect and quantify bacteria within bioaerosols.

pmc-13166862.title: Curative effect of acupuncture combined with Chinese medicine on cancer pain: Systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13166862.creator: Guocheng Xue, Siqi Zhang, Afeng Miao, Yubo Teng, Hao Ming, Miao Zhang
pmc-13166862.description: Background:Cancer and cancer pain caused by treatment have brought great challenges. With the increasing number of papers on the treatment of cancer pain with acupuncture combined with Chinese medicine, this paper aims to evaluate the evidence of the association of acupuncture combined with Chinese medicine with reduction in cancer pain.
